Silicon Valley Bank, which had about $209 billion in assets, collapsed after rising interest rates triggered at least $4.52 billion in losses in its investment portfolio. This led to a bank run, disrupting many technology startups whose deposits it held. The bulk of the bank’s deposits were uninsured.
